items_missed: Never asked 'how are you today?' or any warm-up. The open was 'Hello good afternoon nine Stein moving this is how can I help?' straight into 'when are you planning moving? So we can check availability.'

Agenda statement was present in substance ('I just need to ask you some information in order for me to walk you through how our pricing works and give you the full estimate to start with') but carried no timeframe and no 'sound good?' confirmation — she ended it with 'Can you, go ahead' and started probing.

Customer's name never used once. He gave it clearly — 'the last name is Coats. And my name is Manny' — and she then mis-read the record ('Mary. Okay, hold on.') and never said 'Manny' again for the remaining 25 minutes. Zero of the 3+ standard.

No zip codes captured at any of the three locations — street addresses only, including 'Casa. Anna, second word is and that's in Fluger. Hille,' which she accepted without spelling it back or confirming a zip on a Pflugerville destination that drives the trip fee.

Packing services never offered or priced. The customer opened the door directly — 'when they bring everything in, will they unpack things too if we want' — and she answered only what Einstein does not do ('We don't unpack things like putting the quotes into the dressers') without ever pitching packing service at the same hourly rate plus materials.

Moving stressors never asked. No version of 'is there anything you're particularly worried about with this move?' on a call where the customer was clearly anxious about capacity — he asked unprompted 'what happens if a 26 foot truck can't fit everything?' and 'I definitely want to start early just in case.'

Additional rooms never probed proactively at the apartment. The garage at the 4800 address only surfaced because the customer volunteered it ('we're just moving stuff out of the garage'); she never asked about garage, patio, balcony, or storage closet at mom's two-bedroom.

Square footage was revised upward mid-call and the estimate was never re-run. He first said '1100 or 1200,' then later 'I think it's twelve or 1300. I don't know if that makes a difference or not if it's 1300,' and she answered 'No problem, because 26 foot box truck can't [can] fit in 1700 square foot home' — she answered a truck-capacity question with a time-estimate question outstanding, and the 4.5–5.5 hour figure was never revisited.

Elevator, walk distance, and specialty items were captured but never explained as time variables. She asked 'what's the walk distance from where we can park the truck to the bottom of the elevator,' he said 'I'm not sure, I don't... I have no idea,' and she said 'Oh, okay, no problem' — a 5th-floor apartment with an unknown carry and a reserved elevator went into the quote with no 'if the carry is long, that adds time' framing.

The item list was left as an open loop. 'Okay, do you have the list of items that we're moving so we can be able to put a notification?' / 'I do not. I can make a list though.' She never asked him to send it, never set a deadline, and never told him where to send it — and he was still unsure at the end which living-room tables were even going ('might not be going, but I just wanted to give you more than not enough').

Save Your Ass speech was one line, not the speech. She got the why — 'Just to remove some of the items from the dressers for example. Then that would really help to keep the time down and efficiency up. Obviously the [less] time you take the less money end up spending by the end of the day' — but gave only one consolidation example and no others (kids' toys, garden tools, loose items in drawers, photos off walls).
No 'take a carload' tip — an obvious fit on a job with 'six or seven pieces' out of a garage, small nightstands, and a lamp.
No 'does that make sense?' close after the prep/efficiency section. The only sense-check landed earlier, after the clock explanation ('Does that make sense?' / 'It does, yeah').

Confirmation email described but not framed. Two emails were sent and 'in case I have putt incorrect it does let me know so I can have it amended' covers reply-with-corrections, but the BOLDED key-details list at the top of the email was never mentioned.
No 'any other questions before I let you go?' The customer had to interrupt her own send to get his last two questions in: 'Oh, sorry. I have one question.'
Hours never given. 'You can always email, call us or text us at anytime' names the channels but not the actual business hours.

60¢/lb baseline never mentioned alongside No Worries — the insurance explanation was one-sided, and this was a job with marble/alabaster statues and a marble table insert where the coverage ceiling matters.

Heavy dead air and audibility breakdowns. At least a dozen 'give me one sec' / 'hold on' / 'bear with me' pauses, and the customer reported losing her three separate times: 'What was the question about the address?', 'You cut out. What was the question if?', and 'What was, what was the, you cut out a couple of times.'
AM/PM stated wrong repeatedly on the booking windows — 'we can start 12:30 AM to 1:00 PM' and 'from 12:30 AM to 1:00 PM' — on the one detail the customer most needs to be right in writing.
top_strength: The pricing and differentiator block was near-textbook, and she delivered it on a genuinely awkward three-location job. She opened it correctly — 'let me explain how our pricing works then it is super simple' — landed the rate ('$104 per hour per mover'), the full inclusion list ('the gas, the trucks, the taxes and insurance all the wraps, the pods, the bunds to protect your item... and all of the tools for disassemble and [re]assembly of furniture and appliances'), and then handled the hardest part of this quote well: she scoped the trip fee to the specific leg it applied to and proactively told him where it did not apply — 'There's a trip fee of $115 only because... it's like 45 minutes drive from the first location going to the second location... for your mom's address, there's no trip fee because it's near the new location.' All three differentiators followed in sequence (No Worries $2,000, Meet Your Mover with the correct 'help [ease] the tension of strangers arriving at the front door' reasoning, and the On-Time Guarantee), then the full clock explanation — on-site start at contract open, 2.5-hour minimum, 15-minute prorated increments — closed with 'Does that make sense?' That is a clean 18/20 pricing and a perfect 4/4 clock. She also structured a messy job correctly: two pickups, one destination, two trucks, same day, priced separately, and she took the customer's own two-truck suggestion and confirmed it rather than forcing a single-truck route. Her booking close was real, not implied: 'there's no deposit required. Anyway, there's no risk and securing your spot... Would you like me to lock that in for you?' — and she landed two booked moves with a date change absorbed mid-call without friction.
coaching_note: Highest-leverage fix is the Save Your Ass speech, because on this specific job it was worth real money and she gave one sentence of it. This was a garage clear-out plus a two-bedroom fifth-floor apartment full of small loose items — nightstands with drawers, a hutch with 'little drawers on it that you could put in,' end tables, a lamp, six dining chairs, and a set of alabaster figures. After she gave the 4.5–5.5 hour range she needed to say: 'Manny, here's how you take an hour off that bill. Everything in the nightstand and hutch drawers goes into boxes before we get there, the statues get boxed or grouped in one spot so we're not making twelve trips, and anything you can carry — the lamp, the small tables, the loose stuff — take a carload over yourself the night before. Every trip my guys don't make is fifteen minutes you don't pay for. Does that make sense?' That single paragraph is the difference between a 4/10 and a 10/10 in the section that most moves actual move efficiency. Second priority, and this one is an estimate-accuracy issue Amanda should care about: the square footage changed and the quote did not. He said 1100–1200, then later 'I think it's twelve or 1300,' and she replied 'No problem' and answered a truck-capacity question instead. The correct move was 'Let me update that to 1,300 — that shifts my estimate to X to Y hours, so let's plan on the higher end.' Same failure with the unknown carry distance at a fifth-floor unit: 'I have no idea' should have produced 'That's my biggest unknown, so I'm building in the longer carry and I'll note it for the crew,' not 'Oh, okay, no problem.' Third, use his name — she took it, mis-read it as 'Mary,' and never used it once in 27 minutes, which is why an otherwise competent call reads cold. Two business risks to close in EMMA today: (1) the item list is unowned — he offered 'I can make a list though' and no one asked for it, on a job where he himself does not know which living-room tables are going, so the load plan for a 26-foot truck is guesswork; (2) the booking windows were stated as '12:30 AM to 1:00 PM' more than once, so verify both confirmation emails read 12:30 PM before he replies to change the date, which he told her he was about to do ('I'll call her right now after we're done and then I'll respond to the emails').
phone_presence_notes: Patient and consistently pleasant through a complicated three-address job — 'Oh, okay, no worries,' 'thank you so much for clarifying and bear with me' — but zero name use, no rapport or humor moment, a dozen 'give me one sec' pauses, and a flat 'Oh, okay, no problem' when he admitted he had no idea about the carry distance kept it transactional rather than warm.
audio_review_reason: The customer reported losing her three separate times ('You cut out. What was the question if?'), and her side of the transcript is heavily garbled in exactly the scripted stretches — 'nine Stein moving,' 'early rate,' 'meter mover feature,' 'no sterile fees,' 'Raj I can see collection,' 'deep drivers now pathways' — so it cannot be determined from text whether the clarity/pace deduction reflects her delivery or the line and the transcription. Audio also needed to confirm whether she actually said 12:30 PM rather than the transcribed 12:30 AM.
